title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #11

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What do fish use to take oxygen from water? (1 mark)
   A. Horns
   B. Gills
   C. Feathers
   D. Lungs

2. Which of these is a mammal that lives in water? (1 mark)
   A. Crocodile
   B. Frog
   C. Tilapia
   D. Whale

3. Which group of animals has dry, scaly skin and includes snakes and crocodiles? (1 mark)
   A. Reptiles
   B. Birds
   C. Mammals
   D. Amphibians

4. Which of these animals has a soft body covered by a hard shell? (1 mark)
   A. Snail
   B. Hen
   C. Goat
   D. Ant

5. How many legs does an insect have? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Six
   C. Four
   D. Ten

6. Which of these can you use to find out the differences between vertebrates and invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Books and digital sources
   B. Noise
   C. Only guesses
   D. Weather

7. Which of these do animals breathe in from the air? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Oxygen
   C. Dust
   D. Smoke

8. Which of these is the best question to ask first when you sort an animal into vertebrate or invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Does it have a backbone?
   B. Is it fast?
   C. Is it dangerous?
   D. Is it big?

9. Which of these is a safe thing to do on a science walk? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   B. Pick up unknown snakes
   C. Tease insects
   D. Throw stones at birds

10. A pupil has hard dry faeces. Which is the best advice? (1 mark)
   A. Stop drinking water
   B. Eat only white bread
   C. Eat more sweets
   D. Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water

11. What does the stomach do to food? (1 mark)
   A. Cuts it into pieces
   B. Stores faeces
   C. Takes back water
   D. Churns it and mixes it with juices

12. Why should fruits and vegetables be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To make them sweeter
   B. To remove dirt and germs
   C. To make them hot
   D. To make them heavier

13. What is the solid waste passed out through the anus called? (1 mark)
   A. Faeces
   B. Juice
   C. Saliva
   D. Blood

14. What do teeth do in digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Digest food into the blood
   B. Take back water
   C. Store waste
   D. Cut and grind food into small pieces

15. Which part of the digestive system is long and coiled? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Mouth
   C. Gullet
   D. Small intestine

16. What is digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing away food
   B. Storing food in the stomach for years
   C. Making food hot
   D. Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use

17. Which of these do we drink to keep digestion healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Clean safe water
   C. Sugary drinks all the time
   D. Muddy water

18. Which of these is a solid? (1 mark)
   A. Air
   B. A stone
   C. Milk
   D. Steam

19. Which of these is true of a gas? (1 mark)
   A. It is always visible
   B. It cannot spread out
   C. It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   D. It keeps its own shape

20. Which of these is true of a solid? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be measured
   B. It takes the shape of any container
   C. It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   D. It has no mass

21. What should you wear when collecting waste? (1 mark)
   A. A hat only
   B. Nothing
   C. Sandals only
   D. Gloves and closed shoes

22. Which of these is a tool for picking up waste safely? (1 mark)
   A. A rake
   B. Bare feet
   C. Bare hands
   D. A towel

23. Which is an example of recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Using a tin for a pencil holder
   B. Melting scrap metal to make new items
   C. Throwing paper in a bin
   D. Buying less food

24. Which item is a paper waste that can be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bottle
   B. Glass bottle
   C. Banana peel
   D. Old newspapers

25. Why is broken glass on the ground dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It grows
   B. It can cut people and animals
   C. It rots
   D. It feeds the soil

26. A leaking pipe wastes 5 litres each day. How much is wasted in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 70 litres
   B. 12 litres
   C. 57 litres
   D. 35 litres

27. Why should you keep drinking water in a clean covered container? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it safe from germs
   B. To make it colder
   C. To make it hot
   D. To make it salty

28. Where should a water conservation poster be put? (1 mark)
   A. Under a bed
   B. In a cupboard
   C. In a bin
   D. Near a tap or the school gate

29. Which of these holds objects together? (1 mark)
   A. A rolling ball
   B. A smooth floor
   C. Oil
   D. Glue

30. Where are ball bearings found? (1 mark)
   A. In a pencil
   B. In a book
   C. In bicycle wheels
   D. In a cup

31. Which of these holds a shirt together? (1 mark)
   A. A rolling wheel
   B. Oil
   C. Thread stitches
   D. Wind

32. Which of these is a way of reducing friction on a bicycle chain? (1 mark)
   A. Oiling it
   B. Leaving it dry and rusty
   C. Adding sand
   D. Wetting it with mud

33. Logs placed under a heavy load help it move because they act as (1 mark)
   A. Rollers
   B. Brakes
   C. Weights
   D. Glue

34. Which of these is a way of making a room lighter during the day? (1 mark)
   A. Opening the curtains
   B. Closing the door
   C. Painting the walls black
   D. Closing the window

35. Which of these is transparent? (1 mark)
   A. Clear glass
   B. Metal
   C. Thick cardboard
   D. Wood

36. Which of these is an artificial source of light? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. Electric bulb
   C. Lightning
   D. Stars

37. Which of these uses heat to change dough into bread? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting
   B. Baking
   C. Freezing
   D. Washing

38. Which project helps you to handle hot pots safely? (1 mark)
   A. Making a dustbin
   B. Making a toy
   C. Making a poster
   D. Making kitchen gloves

39. In the water cycle, what does heat from the sun do? (1 mark)
   A. Removes all water
   B. Makes water heavy
   C. Turns water into vapour
   D. Freezes water

40. Which use of heat helps farmers to store maize? (1 mark)
   A. Drying grain
   B. Making shadows
   C. Writing
   D. Colouring paper

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe what happens in the small intestine and why it is important. (4 marks)

42. Explain the importance of conserving water at home and school. (5 marks)

43. Give four ways in which heat is used in farming. (4 marks)

44. What is meant by water conservation? (2 marks)

45. State two reasons for conserving water. (2 marks)

46. Explain why light is important in our daily lives. (5 marks)

47. Describe three examples each of reducing and reusing water. (4 marks)

48. A block is pulled along a rough floor and along a smooth floor with the same force. Describe and explain what you would see. (4 marks)

49. Give three ways of protecting water sources. (3 marks)

50. Explain how wet clothes dry in the sun. (3 marks)

51. A pupil pulls up a small bean plant from the garden. Describe what she will see and give the job of each part she sees. (5 marks)

52. Describe how a pupil can tell that an earthworm is an animal. (3 marks)

53. Give two examples each of transparent and opaque materials. (2 marks)

54. Give three ways of saving water at home. (3 marks)

55. Explain why cooking pots are made of metal but their handles are not. (4 marks)

56. A jug has 1 litre of juice. 350 ml is poured into a cup. How much is left in the jug? (3 marks)

57. Why should you wear gloves when collecting waste? (2 marks)

58. State any four signs of life in animals. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Gills
   Fish breathe using gills.

2. D — Whale
   A whale breathes air and feeds milk to its calf, so it is a mammal even though it lives in water.

3. A — Reptiles
   Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

4. A — Snail
   A snail has a soft body with a shell on its back.

5. B — Six
   All adult insects have six legs.

6. A — Books and digital sources
   We can search print and digital media for information.

7. B — Oxygen
   Animals need oxygen from the air or water.

8. A — Does it have a backbone?
   The backbone decides the group.

9. A — Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   Handling animals safely and washing hands avoids injury and germs.

10. D — Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water
   Fibre and water help soften faeces.

11. D — Churns it and mixes it with juices
   The stomach churns food into a thick soup with digestive juices.

12. B — To remove dirt and germs
   Washing removes dirt, germs and worm eggs.

13. A — Faeces
   Faeces are the solid waste of the body.

14. D — Cut and grind food into small pieces
   Chewing makes food smaller.

15. D — Small intestine
   The small intestine is a very long coiled tube.

16. D — Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   Digestion breaks food into tiny parts that can pass into the blood.

17. B — Clean safe water
   Clean safe water helps digestion and prevents disease.

18. B — A stone
   A stone keeps its shape.

19. C — It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   A gas spreads to fill the space.

20. C — It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   A solid has a definite shape.

21. D — Gloves and closed shoes
   Gloves and shoes protect from cuts and germs.

22. A — A rake
   A rake or shovel keeps hands away from the waste.

23. B — Melting scrap metal to make new items
   Melting metal to make new items is recycling.

24. D — Old newspapers
   Paper can be turned into new paper.

25. B — It can cut people and animals
   Sharp glass can injure.

26. D — 35 litres
   5 x 7 = 35 litres.

27. A — To keep it safe from germs
   Covered clean containers protect water.

28. D — Near a tap or the school gate
   Posters should be seen by many people.

29. D — Glue
   Glue, nails and ropes use forces to hold things together.

30. C — In bicycle wheels
   Bicycle wheels use ball bearings.

31. C — Thread stitches
   Stitches hold cloth pieces together.

32. A — Oiling it
   Oil helps parts slide.

33. A — Rollers
   Rollers reduce friction.

34. A — Opening the curtains
   Open curtains let in more daylight.

35. A — Clear glass
   Clear glass lets light through.

36. B — Electric bulb
   Bulbs are made by people.

37. B — Baking
   Baking uses heat.

38. D — Making kitchen gloves
   Gloves protect hands.

39. C — Turns water into vapour
   Heat causes evaporation from seas and rivers.

40. A — Drying grain
   Heat dries wet things.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Digestion is finished there. Digested food passes through the wall into the blood. The blood carries it to all parts of the body for energy, growth and repair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: There is enough water for all, we save money, animals and crops get water, it reduces work of fetching water and protects sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason up to 5.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drying grain and crops, hatching chicks, keeping chicks warm, cooking, controlling pests, drying fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Using water carefully and protecting water sources so that there is enough for everyone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for careful use and 1 mark for protecting or enough for everyone.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: To have enough water for all, to save money, for crops and animals, to protect sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: It lets us see, keeps us safe, helps plants to make food, dries clothes, gives solar power and discourages pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: close taps, fix leaks, use a cup. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants, laundry water for mopping, rainwater for the garden.
   Working / marking points: Award marks for correct examples up to a total of 4.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: The block moves slower or a shorter distance on the rough floor. Rough floors give more friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees near rivers, do not throw waste in water, do not wash in springs, keep animals away from drinking sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Heat from the sun makes the water evaporate. It changes to vapour and goes into the air so the clothes become dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sun heat, 1 mark for evaporation, 1 mark for the result.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: She will see roots that hold the plant and take in water, a stem that holds it up and carries food and water, leaves that make food, and maybe flowers or pods that make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming each of four parts and 1 mark for correct function overall.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds on soil, grows, breathes, moves, responds to touch, reproduces and removes waste. It shows the signs of life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign, up to 3.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Transparent: clear glass, clear plastic, clean water. Opaque: wood, metal, stone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, use a cup or basin, fix leaks, use a bucket instead of a hose, reuse washing water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Metal passes heat quickly to the food so it cooks. Handles made of wood or plastic pass heat slowly so our hands do not burn.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the pot and 2 marks for the handle.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1 litre = 1000 ml, 1 mark for the subtraction 1000 - 350 and 1 mark for the answer.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect your hands from cuts and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cuts and 1 mark for germs.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Feeding, growing, breathing, reproducing, removing waste, moving, responding to changes, dying (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four.
